solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, directions as headed); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Troop train

definitions.meaning: a troop is a group of animals
to train someone is to teach or educate them

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a collective noun for a band of creatures, and a verb meaning to instruct or drill.

clue.text: Strike 19 notice

definitions.meaning: to ... someone is to hit them
19 points to the answer at 19 across; to ... a runner is to measure how long they take

explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: a slangy punch, measuring a duration with a stopwatch, and spotting something; it is also Haydn's Symphony No. 101.

clue.text: Work through duck and hen supply, overseeing one article for Paris connoisseur

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first pieces sit above, or oversee, what follows

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, the letter O

indicators.note: the work runs through the middle of the shuffled hen
supply read as supple, i.e. bendy, so the letters of hen are worked into a new order

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
the Roman numeral for one
le is a French definite article

explanation.surface: A wine buff in Paris oversees a farmyard supply of poultry while working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun, but it is read as the adjective supple (pronounced 'supply'), meaning bendy, which is why it can signal an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: This word names an expert taster of wine, a particular kind of connoisseur.

clue.text: Is successful story at Birmingham Weight Watchers this idle?

indicators.note: the tale as told in a Birmingham (Brummie) accent, where the vowel of light comes out as loit

parts.note: what someone who is successful at a slimming club becomes is lighter

explanation.surface: A slimmer wonders whether success at their Birmingham weight-loss group is just a lazy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Weight Watchers is a slimming club. The Birmingham (Brummie) accent turns the 'eye' sound into 'oy', so 'lighter' said there matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to hang around doing nothing, a synonym of the answer as a verb.

clue.text: Work I say succeeded, going over fake

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

indicators.note: going over means turned over, so the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: my is an exclamation of surprise like 'I say!'
phony means fake

explanation.surface: A man reports that something succeeded only by passing over a forgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony is an orchestral composition, an example of a musical work or opus.

clue.text: Vassal's fun with Viola in play, part of what comes from the heart

definitions.text: part of what comes from the heart

indicators.note: a play rearranges the action, so these letters are acted out in a new order

explanation.surface: A servant has fun with Viola, the heroine of Twelfth Night, during a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Viola is a character in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, which steers you towards the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: These are bulges at the root of the aorta, the great artery leaving the heart, so they are part of it.

clue.text: Soldiers on, breaching target over railroad

indicators.note: breaching means breaking into, so one piece goes inside the other
over means turned over, so the target word is read backwards

parts.note: an aim is a target
a light that is on is lit
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Troops press on, breaking through to a target across the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Collectively the armed forces, soldiers as a body; also Haydn's Symphony No. 100.

clue.text: 101 & 45 his, among others here, not comin' out for listeners?

indicators.note: for an audience hearing it, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: staying out of sight, in dropped-g speech, is hidin'

explanation.surface: Someone who stays indoors still has a couple of numbered works played for an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Symphonies 101 (the Clock) and 45 (the Farewell) are his, and many of his symphony nicknames fill this grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer wrote the Clock and Farewell symphonies, numbered 101 and 45, and many others named in the grid.

clue.text: Am then picking up Scary Spice — it's easy

indicators.note: then puts the next piece after the first

parts.note: am is short for amateur, someone who is no pro

indicators.note: picking up means lifting, so in a down clue the name is read upwards

parts.note: Scary Spice of the Spice Girls is Mel B

explanation.surface: An amateur picks up a Spice Girls tune and finds it simple.
explanation.walkthrough: Scary Spice was Melanie Brown of the 1990s British pop group the Spice Girls, known as Mel B.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal reassurance that a task is simple and causes no trouble.

clue.text: Iron's dissolving in mercury secure? I missed warning

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the symbol

parts.note: Hg is the chemical symbol for mercury

indicators.note: dissolving breaks the word apart, so its letters are reformed in a new order
the clue's 'I missed' says the letter I is left out of the fastening word

parts.note: to nail something is to secure it

explanation.surface: A chemist reports iron dissolving in mercury and admits missing the warning signs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dissolving' rearranges IRONS to ORNSI, placed in HG; 'I missed' takes I from NAIL to leave NAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast on a horn is a warning signal; also the nickname of Haydn's Symphony No. 31.

clue.text: See reclining seats one's putting out with them?

indicators.note: seats means holds within, so one letter sits inside
reclining means lying back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to spy is to see
one gives the Roman numeral I; the 's (is) runs on to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone looks at the reclining seats and asks if they are being put out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reclining' turns SPY round to YPS, which holds I. The definition is about golf: putting is gentle strokes on the green, and the yips are a nervous twitch that ruins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The yips are a golfer's attack of nerves on short putts, so one putts out suffering from them.

clue.text: We're leaving out butterflies

definitions.meaning: people who leave things out skip them, so 'we' are those who skip
a family of small, darting butterflies bears this name

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is people who omit or miss things; the other is a family of small brown butterflies with darting flight.

clue.text: Don't stop nursing what athlete's overstretched?

parts.note: to tend a patient is to nurse them
to go on, or carry on, is not to stop

explanation.surface: A plea to keep caring for an injured athlete who has pulled something.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, 'tend on' would mean carry on nursing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord linking muscle to bone is the classic sports injury when a runner strains it.

clue.text: Showed Island Queen

parts.note: a paper that ran a story showed it

explanation.surface: A queen from an island put herself on display.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is an Indian queen or a rajah's wife.

clue.text: Here, everyone (bar one) preparing miracle little solution

indicators.note: bar means except, so the numeral is taken out of the mixed letters
preparing means making up, so the letters are mixed into something new

parts.note: SOL is a shortened form of solution (soln)
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A chemist cooks up a small miracle cure for nearly everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preparing' mixes MIRACLE and SOL, and 'bar one' says an I is left out of that mix. Haydn's Symphony No. 96 is the Miracle, so 'Here' points to the grid's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means anyone who turns up, i.e. all comers taken together.

clue.text: Leaving do ahead of spring

indicators.note: ahead of puts the first piece before the next

parts.note: to do well or badly is to fare
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: A leaving party arranged just before springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving do' reads as a party, but the definition is 'Leaving' alone; 'do' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell is a parting or departure; also Haydn's Symphony No. 45.

clue.text: Notifies people to stay true to burst boilers

indicators.note: the word for notifying lets other letters stay inside it

parts.note: to warn someone is to notify them

indicators.note: to burst is to break apart, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A notice tells residents to stay put, true to form, because the boilers have burst.
explanation.definitionFit: These large metal vessels heat water for tea, so they are boilers.

clue.text: Rotisserie cooks put in request for vacation with just a hint of sarcasm

indicators.note: to cook the books is to tamper with them, so these letters are tampered into a new order
vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters of the word stay
a hint is a trace, so only the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: Chefs sarcastically submit a holiday request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for vacation' empties REQUEST to RT, and 'just a hint of' takes S from SARCASM.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating spit for roasting meat over a fire, which is what a rotisserie is.

clue.text: Like non-standard, occasionally-used, musical expression of praise

indicators.note: non means without, so the norm is dropped from the front

parts.note: parallel means alike or corresponding
par is a standard, as in golf

indicators.note: occasionally means here and there, so only every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A description of an unusual, rarely used piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-standard' removes PAR from PARALLEL to leave ALLEL, and 'occasionally-used' takes UIA from MUSICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternative form of hallelujah, a shout of praise to God sung in hymns; also Haydn's Symphony No. 30.

clue.text: Dimension of centimetre in wall of heart

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the walls of the middle-meaning word, so taking those walls away leaves them

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre

explanation.surface: A measurement in centimetres taken from the heart wall.
explanation.walkthrough: CENTIMETRE is CENTRE with the answer's letters set in its walls, so removing CENTRE leaves them.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists treat duration as the fourth dimension alongside length, breadth and height; also Haydn's Le Midi.

clue.text: Checker of movement of renumbered bottles

indicators.note: bottles means contains, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of moving things checks the relabelled bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' is a verb meaning holds, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: This fold of tissue, such as the one under the tongue, restrains the movement of the organ it holds.

clue.text: Here M40 leads Oxford type, say, learner ahead to West

indicators.note: to the West means on the left, so these pieces go before the next

parts.note: L is the learner plate on British cars
to go on is to go ahead
a don is a university teacher, as at Oxford

explanation.surface: Directions on the M40 motorway, which leads from Oxford, with a learner driver ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The M40 is the motorway joining Birmingham and Oxford to the capital. Haydn's last symphony, No. 104, is nicknamed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The M40 motorway runs south-east to the capital of England, so it leads there.

clue.text: Drumroll occasionally cut short by Royal Engraver

indicators.note: cut short means docked, so the last letter of the pick goes
occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the royal Queen

explanation.surface: A drum roll now and then interrupted by a royal engraver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes DURL from DRUMROLL and 'cut short' drops its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was the German Renaissance master of the woodcut and copper engraving.

clue.text: In dawn run, philosopher's first to overcome new shock

indicators.note: overcome means to replace or beat, so the new letter gives way to others

parts.note: sunrise is dawn
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the thinker is used

explanation.surface: A philosopher out on a dawn run is overcome by a sudden fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to overcome' swaps the N in SUNRISE for R plus P. The Philosopher (No. 22) and Surprise (No. 94) are both Haydn symphonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise is an unexpected event that startles, a sudden jolt.

clue.text: Monsieur bathing in a little French river

indicators.note: the abbreviation bathes inside the other word, so it goes within it

parts.note: some means a little

explanation.surface: A Frenchman takes a brief dip in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme flows through northern France, famous for the First World War battle.

clue.text: Carry, as echo in pub

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the drinking place

parts.note: a bar is a pub
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Carrying something, as an echo carries through a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a load is to carry it; also Haydn's Symphony No. 82.

clue.text: Amicus inspiring daughter Hannah?

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the letter is taken inside

parts.note: amicus is Latin for friend, so a pal in Rome

explanation.surface: A friend inspires a girl named Hannah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hannah?' is a definition by example: the name reads the same backwards. The query marks that.
explanation.definitionFit: The name Hannah is spelt identically from either end, the defining property of such a word.

clue.text: Empress up a street doing U-turn

indicators.note: doing a U-turn means turning back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: astir means up and about

explanation.surface: An empress up the street turns her carriage round.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of a tsar, a Russian empress.

clue.text: Original depiction of mother in labour (it's a boy!)?

indicators.note: a mother in labour carries her baby, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: mater is Latin, and old public-school slang, for mother
a boy is a son, abbreviated S

explanation.surface: A painting of a mother giving birth announces the baby is a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: With 1 across it makes the Schoolmaster, Haydn's Symphony No. 55.
explanation.definitionFit: A master is the original recording or document from which copies are made.
